Search syzkaller descriptions for timeval usage patterns: $ grep -R "struct timeval" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux | head -n 20; grep -R "timeval\b" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux | head -n 20; grep -R "^timeval" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux | head -n 20

Look for per-arch constants patterns in syzkaller .const files: $ grep -R "^arches" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/*.const | head -n 20 && awk 'NR<=80{print}' /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/socket.txt.const | sed -n '1,80p' && echo '---' && grep -R "\[amd64\]" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/*.const | head -n 20
Find .const files that repeat arches lines for per-arch values: $ grep -R "^arches =" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/*.const | awk -F: '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head

Inspect syzkaller const file parser for per-arch support: $ grep -R "type Const" -n /opt/syzkaller/pkg/compiler | head -n 20 && grep -R "arches" -n /opt/syzkaller/pkg/compiler | head -n 50 && grep -R "parseConst" -n /opt/syzkaller/pkg/compiler | head -n 50
Open const_file.go to understand arch-specific constant syntax: $ sed -n '200,340p' /opt/syzkaller/pkg/compiler/const_file.go

Compute ppdev ioctl numbers for amd64 and 386 sizes: $ python3 - <<'PY' import struct  def ioc(dir_, type_, nr, size):     return (dir_<<30) | (size<<16) | (type_<<8) | nr  def _io(type_, nr):     return ioc(0,type_,nr,0)  def _ior(type_, nr, size):     return ioc(2,type_,nr,size)  def _iow(type_, nr, size):     return ioc(1,type_,nr,size)  PP_IOCTL=ord('p')  # sizes sizeof_int=4 sizeof_uint=4 sizeof_uchar=1 sizeof_frob=2 sizeof_timeval_amd64=16 sizeof_timeval_386=8  ioctls = {  'PPSETMODE': ('w',0x80,'int'),  'PPRSTATUS': ('r',0x81,'uchar'),  # PPWSTATUS obsolete  'PPRCONTROL': ('r',0x83,'uchar'),  'PPWCONTROL': ('w',0x84,'uchar'),  'PPFCONTROL': ('w',0x8e,'frob'),  'PPRDATA': ('r',0x85,'uchar'),  'PPWDATA': ('w',0x86,'uchar'),  # obsolete: PPRECONTROL 0x87, PPWECONTROL 0x88, PPRFIFO 0x89, PPWFIFO 0x8a  'PPCLAIM': ('',0x8b,None),  'PPRELEASE': ('',0x8c,None),  'PPYIELD': ('',0x8d,None),  'PPEXCL': ('',0x8f,None),  'PPDATADIR': ('w',0x90,'int'),  'PPNEGOT': ('w',0x91,'int'),  'PPWCTLONIRQ': ('w',0x92,'uchar'),  'PPCLRIRQ': ('r',0x93,'int'),  'PPSETPHASE': ('w',0x94,'int'),  'PPGETTIME': ('r',0x95,'timeval'),  'PPSETTIME': ('w',0x96,'timeval'),  'PPGETMODES': ('r',0x97,'uint'),  'PPGETMODE': ('r',0x98,'int'),  'PPGETPHASE': ('r',0x99,'int'),  'PPGETFLAGS': ('r',0x9a,'int'),  'PPSETFLAGS': ('w',0x9b,'int'), }  sizes = {  'int': sizeof_int,  'uint': sizeof_uint,  'uchar': sizeof_uchar,  'frob': sizeof_frob,  'timeval': None,  None: 0 }  for arch, timeval_sz in [('amd64',sizeof_timeval_amd64),('386',sizeof_timeval_386)]:     out = {}     for name,(dirc,nr,typ) in ioctls.items():         if dirc=='':             val=_io(PP_IOCTL,nr)         elif dirc=='r':             sz = timeval_sz if typ=='timeval' else sizes[typ]             val=_ior(PP_IOCTL,nr,sz)         elif dirc=='w':             sz = timeval_sz if typ=='timeval' else sizes[typ]             val=_iow(PP_IOCTL,nr,sz)         else:             raise         out[name]=val     print(arch)     for k in sorted(out):         print(f"{k} = {out[k]} (0x{out[k]:x})")     print() PY
Inspect existing syz_open_dev patterns for numbered device nodes: $ grep -R "string\[\"/dev/.*#\"\]" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/dev_*.txt | head -n 40
Check existing ioctl descriptions for _IO no-argument pattern: $ grep -R "arg const\[0\]" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux | grep "ioctl\$" | head -n 30

Find ioctl descriptions that take intptr or 0 for _IO commands: $ grep -R "TIOCNOTTY" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux | head -n 20 && grep -R "ioctl\$.*const\[.*\], arg" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/tty.txt | head -n 40
View an existing device description file as a template: $ sed -n '1,120p' /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/dev_i2c.txt

Check whether ppdev/parport headers exist in syzkaller include paths: $ ls -la /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/include/linux/ppdev.h /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/include/linux/parport.h /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/include/uapi/linux/ppdev.h /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/include/uapi/linux/parport.h 2>/dev/null || true; find /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/include -maxdepth 3 -name 'ppdev.h' -o -name 'parport.h'

Locate the uapi headers referenced by existing syzlang files: $ grep -R "include <uapi/linux/i2c-dev.h>" -n /opt/syzkaller/sys/linux/dev_i2c.txt && find /opt/syzkaller -path '*uapi/linux/i2c-dev.h' | head && find /opt/syzkaller -path '*linux/ppdev.h' | head && find /opt/syzkaller -path '*linux/parport.h' | head
Explore syzkaller directory structure to locate include headers: $ find /opt/syzkaller -maxdepth 3 -type d -print | head -n 50
Locate syzkaller sys directory and its include/header subdirs: $ ls -la /opt/syzkaller/sys && find /opt/syzkaller/sys -maxdepth 3 -type d -print | head -n 80
